obs_text: 'find' is here an act whose object is the inner being (God searching hearts, the spirit searching the innermost parts), or what is found is an inner state of the other (favour, mercy, rest, enjoyment, cheer); it bears on the inner being without being the operation.

obs_text: In the NT the one who humbles himself is any person. What follows is named as: "justified" (Luk 18:14); "grace" (Jam 4:6); "exalt you … at the proper time" (1Pe 5:6); "rest for your souls" (Mat 11:29).

He is the ground and the example for humility toward others. Phili 2:3–5 makes "in humility count others more significant" rest on "this mind … in Christ Jesus". Also 1Pe 2:21; Eph 5:21; 2Cor 10:1; Mat 11:29.

10.2 The lowly / poor spirit: "Blessed are the poor in spirit" (Mat 5:3) [H1]; "he who is lowly in spirit will obtain honor" (Pro 29:23) [H1]; "It is better to be of a lowly spirit with the poor" (Pro 16:19) [H1]; "a contrite and lowly spirit … to revive the spirit of the lowly" (Isa 57:15) [H1]; "I am gentle and lowly in heart, and you will find rest for your souls" (Mat 11:29) — lowly heart (Jesus) → rest for souls (disciples)

14. Cross-cutting observations for Batch F [Claude reading]: Relating to others is most often a matter of the soul.; Souls are knit (1Sa 18:1).; A soul loves, seeks and fails (Song 3; 5).; Malice lives in the soul (Eze 25:6, 15).; Souls abhor each other, even God's soul and the people's (Lev 26).; One loves another "as one's own soul".; The heart is where hatred starts and is spoken (Lev 19:17; Gen 27:41). It is also where the response to another's fall is judged (Pro 24:17).; The human spirit registers bonds and bearing.; It is unsettled by a friend's absence and refreshed by a friend's arrival (2Co 2:13; 7:13; 1Co 16:18).; It is the manner of approach — gentleness (1Co 4:21).; It is what the wise hold back and the fool vents (Pro 29:11).; Sequences matter more than single verses. Reading before and after changed the picture in six places: 1Sa 18 (Jonathan and Saul); Lev 26 (reciprocal abhorrence broken by God); Psa 143 and Psa 51 (the crushing chains); Judg 19 and the other merry-heart narratives (threshold states); 2Co 2 → 7 (the spirit's rest through persons); 2Ki 2 (spirit transfer confirmed by others); Meaning shifts with circumstance in consistent ways: *crush*: by whom, and turned to whom (§5); *tender heart*: to what it yields (§6); *good heart*: from God or from wine (§7); *love / hate one's soul*: well-being vs clinging (§3); *hāgâ*: what the heart rehearses (§12.2); *nûaḥ*: what rests in or on the person (§9.5); Inner states spread between people: the fainthearted soldier melts others (Deu 20:8); heart-speech is reported (Gen 27:42); a lowly heart gives rest to other souls (Mat 11:29); a congregation refreshes Titus's spirit (2Co 7:13); the prophet's heart takes in the people's doom (Jer 4:18–19); Other spirits relate to people as occupants of a house (Mat 12:43–45) and as seizures between people (1Sa 18:10; Judg 9:23 in Batch D). The divine Spirit rests upon people and is recognised by others (Num 11; 2Ki 2).; Fringe worth keeping: the knit soul beside the seizing spirit in one chapter (1Sa 18); the heart awake while the body lags (Song 5); God refusing to complete reciprocal abhorrence (Lev 26:44); Jezebel curing a vexed spirit by a manufactured good heart (1Ki 21); the prophet's heart for Moab set against Ammon's malice of soul (Isa 15; Jer 48; Eze 25); past hatred as a legal criterion (Deu 19)
